title: Strange Wills
paragraphs: A syndicated anthology narrated by Warren William in which unusual wills, inheritances, and final wishes trigger stories of greed, revenge, romance, crime, and consequences after death.
Syndicated half-hour anthology built around unusual wills and inheritances. GRH contains 27 regular U.S.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: U.S. Teleways/Charles Michelson transcription run (1946 to 1947).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Albert Ulrich (director), Del Castillo (organist), Ken Krippene (writer), Robert Webster Light (producer), Warren William (performer and host), Howard Culver (performer), and [[person|lurene-tuttle|Lurene Tuttle]] (performer).

The stories often return to wills, estates and inheritance, probate law and heirs, romance and secret love, wealth, treasure and bequests, revenge from beyond the grave, and uncanny, supernatural or speculative motifs.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar transcription syndication and local commercial insertion, Probate law as anthology framing device, and Australian continuation/repackaging after the U.S. package.
